answer: Persistent work-history portability. An agent’s reputation is locked to a yarrow-marked ledger entry that only accrues through verified completed transactions, so a fresh clone starts at zero and must re-earn trust from scratch. Every identity also posts a copper settlement deposit that is slashed on any duplicate-behavior detection across the grove of linked accounts, making each clone a separate unrecoverable cost rather than a free copy. An attacker cloning N identities pays N deposits plus N full reputation rebuilds, while an honest agent pays once and carries its history forward.
